mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases uncertainty and risk premia, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% each for two consecutive months signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls > -1% AND HOUST falls > -1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for six consecutive months signals a strong labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly above zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.4% for five consecutive months signals an acceleration in supply capacity, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly positive at 5% significance.
